subtitle: Master the foundation of rock, metal, and punk music with comprehensive power chord techniques and theory

introduction.title: Power Chords (5th Chords)
introduction.text: Power chords are two-note chords consisting of a root note and its perfect fifth. They form the backbone of rock, metal, punk, and many other genres, providing a powerful, driving sound that cuts through dense mixes.

columns.title: Also Known As
columns.text: 5th chords, fifth chords. Notation: Root + "5" (e.g., E5, A5, C5). Structure: Root + Perfect Fifth. Sound: Neutral, powerful, neither major nor minor.

columns.title: Why Power Chords?
columns.text: Distortion-friendly: No third means no muddiness. Easy to play: Simple two-finger shapes. Moveable: Same shape works across the fretboard. Powerful sound: Foundation of rock music. Neutral tonality: Neither major nor minor.

fields.label: Downstrokes
fields.value: Primary technique for power and aggression. Creates consistent attack and tone. Essential for punk and metal styles.

fields.label: Alternate Picking
fields.value: For faster passages and complex rhythms. Down-up-down-up motion. More efficient for speed.

fields.label: Palm Muting
fields.value: Rest palm lightly on strings near bridge. Creates tight, percussive sound. Essential for modern rock/metal.

fields.label: Basic Fingering
fields.value: Index finger on root note. Ring finger on fifth (2 frets higher). Keep fingers curved and close to frets.

fields.label: Muting Technique
fields.value: Use index finger to lightly touch higher strings. Thumb can mute 6th string when playing 5th string root.

fields.label: Octave Addition
fields.value: Add pinky one string higher, same fret as root. Creates fuller, thicker sound. Example: E5 = E(6th) + B(5th) + E(4th).

fields.label: Interval Structure
fields.value: Perfect Fifth interval (7 semitones). Most consonant interval after octave. No third = no major/minor quality.

fields.label: Why No Third?
fields.value: Third creates beating with distortion. Cleaner sound through amplification. Neutral tonality works in any key.

fields.label: Harmonic Function
fields.value: Can function as major or minor chords. Context determines harmonic meaning. Excellent for modal music.

fields.label: Rock & Hard Rock
fields.value: Foundation of classic rock rhythm. Often with moderate distortion. Examples: AC/DC, Led Zeppelin.

fields.label: Metal
fields.value: Heavy distortion and palm muting. Fast, aggressive rhythms. Often in dropped tunings. Examples: Metallica, Black Sabbath.

fields.label: Punk
fields.value: Fast downstrokes, simple progressions. Raw, energetic sound. Examples: Ramones, Sex Pistols.

steps.title: Chord Changes
steps.description: Practice switching between E5, A5, and D5. Start slow, focus on clean changes.

steps.title: Strumming Patterns
steps.description: Use all downstrokes: Down-Down-Up-Down. Keep steady tempo with metronome.

steps.title: Palm Muting
steps.description: Practice same chords with palm muting. Light touch, percussive sound.

steps.title: Advanced: Chromatic Movement & Octave Power Chords
steps.description: Move power chords chromatically up and down the neck. Add the octave note with your pinky for fuller three-note power chords.
